newsitem.title: GERMANY: German commodity bourse plans Q4 live pig contract.
newsitem.headline: German commodity bourse plans Q4 live pig contract.

text.p: The planned German farm futures exchange proposes to start trading a live pig contract in the fourth quarter of 1997, said Michael Hofmann, board member of the holding company Warenterminboerse (WTB) AG.
"We should be able to start with pigs in the fourth quarter but that may not be the right timing for the envisaged wheat contract," he said in response to an enquiry.
The Lower Saxony state government last month approved a WTB application to conduct international electronic futures dealings.
The much-delayed project last summer secured enough bank support to get off the ground.
Preliminary pig contract specifications are for live delivery, but on a basis of 8,000 kg slaughterweight.
A planned wheat contract would be based on 50 tonnes of high quality wheat (11.5 percent protein, 220 hagberg) and several European delivery points.
Potato and rapeseed contracts are planned later on.
Hofmann said WTB would hold two-day training seminars on February 13 and 14 for interested parties in the private and public sectors.
WTB was aiming for some 35 to 50 trading members initially.
Further talks were necessary with potential providers of clearing house functions and trading systems .
